what: Trailing backslash in an @argfile line (e.g. a Windows path C:\dir\) makes tokenize throw StringIndexOutOfBounds instead of reporting "trailing backslash". Reproduced with scala-cli on the copied file.

Scala 2 tokenizes argfiles line by line and throws on a missing file; Scala 3 joins lines then tokenizes once, so an unbalanced quote swallows following lines, and a missing argfile expands to nothing and compilation continues.
unparse emits 2.13.0.-RC1 (spurious dot); unused in compiler/src so no effect today.
COLUMNS="" or non-numeric makes defaultPageWidth throw NumberFormatException while ScalaSettings initialises. Not run.
isMac still tests javaVendor.startsWith("Apple"); always false on modern JDKs. Unused. Copy also lacks isLinux, isJavaAtLeast.
Empty arguments are filtered everywhere, so scala script.sc "" loses the positional argument; Scala 2 only drops empties in option position.

MethodParameters count read with signed nextByte; 128+ parameters give a negative count, the loop runs zero times and the next attribute is parsed from inside this one's payload. Needs javac -parameters and >127 params.

For non-static inner Java classes compiled with -parameters, the outer-instance parameter is stripped from the constructor type but namedParams is indexed by raw MethodParameters position, so parameter names shift by one (param 0 becomes this$0). Affects named arguments to inner-class constructors. Not run.
No read-buffer reuse: a fresh array, ByteBuffer and two streams per classfile. Scala 2 reuses a per-thread buffer. Perf only, unmeasured.
Scala 2 clears FINAL on a class that is also ABSTRACT (Kotlin emits that combination). Scala 3 keeps both flags; consequence uncertain.
<local child> classes and local dummies from Scala 2 pickles are entered into the owner scope; Scala 2 excludes them. No known user-visible failure.

s"" interpolations are rewritten to a left-deep chain of +, one level per part. 500 parts crashes dotc with StackOverflowError (reproduced on 3.7.3: n=100 ok, n=250 crash in a MegaPhase, n=500 in erasure). Scala 2 concatenates in chunks of 32.
f"$d%,,d" compiles and throws DuplicateFormatFlagsException at runtime; Scala 2 reports it at compile time. Reproduced on 3.7.3.
Folded values match Scala 2, but there is no warning for 1/0, Int.MaxValue + 1, Int.MinValue / -1.
An indexed conversion after a splice that refers to a different argument is silently turned into %s; Scala 2 warns. The expected warning only exists in a never-enabled test under tests/untried.
No compile-time shortcut for f"" with no real formatting or all-literal args; always emits runtime StringOps.format. Perf/size only.
Invalid escape in an f"" part is reported on the whole part, not the escape (the s path positions it correctly).
Scaladoc $variable lookup for an object does not search the companion class's @defines; the self-type half of the same Scala 2 commit is present.
Async trace writer catches Exception not Throwable; an Error leaves the status incomplete and close() may hang. Only with -Yprofile-trace; not tested.

s2: n/a: Scala 3 regression from da99eb87b0 (2026-07) "Improve IO package encapsulation"
what: getSubDir now goes through AbstractFile.lookupPath with the trailing-slash package dir name ("p/"); the empty last segment makes it return None. So hasPackage("p") is false and packages("p") is empty for every non-root package, and an aggregate classpath drops the entry for findClassFile("p.q.C"). Reproduced with a Java harness against compiled classes. Root-package classes (REPL wrappers) still work, which hides it.

The process-global FileBasedCache is keyed by jar path only, but the cached ZipArchiveClassPath bakes -release into its versioned JarFile. A second compiler in the same JVM with a different -release (sbt server, Bloop, Metals, cross-builds) gets the first one's multi-release view. Scala 2 added release to the key.

FileZipArchive.close() has no caller; the cache has no refcount, eviction or close path (clear() says "TODO support closing"). Replaced jars stay open until GC; with -Ydisable-flat-cp-caching every Run leaks a ZipFile per jar. Scala 2 threads a CloseableRegistry through PathResolver/ClassPathFactory. Effects: Windows file locks on jars, fd growth in servers, unbounded cache.

With -release N below the running JDK, every ContextBase opens a new zip FileSystem on lib/ct.sym and walks the whole release tree; nothing closes it. Measured: 127 ms first, 16-24 ms after, and lsof shows the handles still open. Scala 2 caches by (release, ct.sym stamp) and closes via the registry.

Cache stamp is (lastModified, fileKey) without file size, so a jar rewritten within one mtime tick keeps a stale index. Also Files.readAttributes throws if the jar vanishes between lookup and create; Scala 2 catches NoSuchFileException.

s2: n/a: regression from da99eb87b0; Scala 2 uses a string baseName
what: Each jar entry name now goes through java.nio.file.Path.of(entryName).getFileName. On Windows an entry containing <>:"|?* or a backslash throws InvalidPathException (unchecked, not caught by SymbolLoader) while indexing the jar. Also one Path allocation per entry on the indexing hot path. Not run on Windows.
JRT classpath is always first, so a user-supplied -javabootclasspath is shadowed; no -Yrelease:sun.misc-style escape for packages hidden by --release, no --system image. Feature gaps.
One shared ZipFile per cached jar; reads synchronize on it under concurrent compilers in one JVM. Scala 2 uses a bounded per-archive pool.

s2: n/a: Scala 3-only change 7f16e81220 (2026-09, #26794 "Warn when catching Errors"); 2.13.x still catches Throwable
what: catch { case t: Throwable => handleFailure(t, ec) } became NonFatal(t). NonFatal excludes InterruptedException, so an interrupt thrown in a Future callback now escapes run on the executor thread and the derived future never completes; the wasInterrupted branch of handleFailure is dead code. Reproduced on 3.10.1-RC1 (first release with the change; 3.10.0 and 2.13.16 fail the future with the InterruptedException): Future.map body interrupted during shutdown leaves the future incomplete, Await times out, onComplete never fires. On parasitic the future also stays incomplete and the interrupt flag is lost. reproducers (gist); reported on #26794.

s2: n/a: same Scala 3 commit 7f16e81220; 2.13.x catches Throwable
what: initState catches only Exception. An Error from the thunk (StackOverflowError from a deep lazy chain, ???, OOM) never restores _tail nor counts down the InRace latch: the same thread then gets the misleading self-reference RuntimeException and other threads hang. Reproduced on 3.10.1-RC1 for ??? in a thunk (second force: bogus self-reference error; other thread blocks forever), for LazyListIterable, and for a StackOverflowError deep in the thunk where a same-thread retry with a smaller limit or a big-stack thread used to succeed. Caveat: when the overflow lands in initState itself the Throwable handler already re-overflowed on 3.10.0. reproducers (gist); reported on #26794.

AsyncBatch.apply/resubmit now use NonFatal; a task throwing InterruptedException or ControlThrowable skips resubmit and the rest of the batch is silently dropped. Reproduced on 3.10.1-RC1 with ExecutionContext.opportunistic: three maps batched, first one interrupted, the other two futures never complete. (global itself does not batch.) reproducers (gist); reported on #26794.
Await.result/ready leaves its CompletionLatch registered on timeout or interrupt, and unregisterCallback does not follow Link. Leak per timed-out await.
transpose takes the row class from the outer array's component type, so a type-changing asArray fails with ArrayStoreException.

s2: reverse: scala3 4a3ecde9cb (#26672) fixed library/; 2.13.x Enumeration.scala:301 still wrong
what: ValueSet.iteratorFrom is wrong for negative ids. Fixed in Scala 3's library/ but not in the full-file Scala.js override, nor forward-ported to 2.13.x.
library-js/src overrides are full-file copies that miss fixes applied to library/: ArrayBuilder still has the removed equals overrides; Enumeration is I8. A second, inner untracked fork.
Still catches the deprecated-for-removal AccessControlException; 2.13 catches SecurityException.
Tail updater uses a lazy val instead of a holder object.

s2: reverse: scala3-only perf/null fixes absent from 2.13.x head
what: Candidates for forward-porting to 2.13.x: HashSet.diff double compute (270f3f274b), HashMap/HashSet concat getHash (8b7e2cec53), HashMap.from empty builder (e3406b0fb1), ArrayDeque.clear O(n) (f36ea50842), ArrayOps.WithFilter.flatMap re-read (7bec039ff4), BitSet.isEmpty allocation (035a05af5b), BoxesRunTime.equalsCharObject null ordering (0c8c581143, b264c1965c).

a(0) = (expr: Nothing) on a primitive array: the value is loaded with no expected type, so scala/runtime/Nothing$ is left on the stack before dastore/iastore and the whole class fails verification. Scala 2 passes elementType so adapt emits ATHROW. Reproduced: VerifyError "Bad type on operand stack" at V0$.f([D)V @9: dastore on 3.10.0; the same source runs on 2.13.16.

Static forwarders for object members get no ACC_DEPRECATED, no MethodParameters (Java and reflection see arg0), no LocalVariableTable, and parameter annotations are dropped (params = Nil with a TODO). Verified with javap. Instance methods are fine.

For a generic inner class of a generic outer, the AppliedType case passes the tycon as pre, so the outer's type args are dropped: Outer[String]#Inner[Int] becomes LOuter$Inner<Integer>; where Scala 2 emits LOuter<String>.Inner<...>;. Existing tests only cover inner classes without their own type params. Diffed on ~25 signature shapes against 2.13.16.
A static field selected through an impure qualifier does not POP the qualifier. Only reachable from macro/plugin trees; Scala 3 source cannot select a Java static through an instance.

s2: n/a: Scala 3-only f831f7df48 (2026-10-16) on top of parallel class writing; Scala 2 1ceafd2275 uses CREATE|TRUNCATE_EXISTING
what: deleteIfExists then CREATE_NEW on pool threads; two classes differing only in case (a warning, not an error) could race to an "Error writing" IOException on case-insensitive filesystems. Not reproduced.

The text-block pre-scan advances a lookahead scanner but the loop guard reads the outer scanner's ch, which never moves. An unclosed Java """ runs off the end: StringIndexOutOfBoundsException from the parser instead of "unclosed text block". Reproduced on the nightly.
No Trojan Source check: U+202A-202E / U+2066-2069 in strings, chars, comments and identifiers compile silently. Scala 2.13.9+ errors. Reproduced.

Form feed counts as a line terminator in the line table, so every later line number shifts by one in diagnostics and in the emitted LineNumberTable. Scala 2 counts only CR/LF/CRLF. Reproduced (error reported at line 5 for physical line 4).
<![CDATA[..]]> becomes Text instead of PCData, so it no longer round-trips; no -Xxml:coalescing equivalent.
case <z>{{3}}</z> gives "pattern expected": the pattern side treats { unconditionally as an embedded pattern; the expression side already uses xCheckEmbeddedBlock. Reproduced.
Java throws clauses from source are discarded, so forwarders to source-parsed Java methods get no Exceptions attribute (classfile-loaded Java methods do, via ThrowsAnnotation). Effect not tested.
Java 7 literals 1_000, 0b101, hex floats silently lose the constant type of a static final, and drop the annotation when used as an argument. Not a missed port; both compilers.

s2: shared gap: scala/scala f9e0b1a03a has the same structure
what: A file whose first declaration is @interface in the default package fails: the leading-annotation prologue consumes @ then fails on interface. Works after package or import.

s2: n/a: port divergence; 2.13 uses a lazy for-comprehension with visited check
what: Strict .filter(!visited(_)).collectFirst lets a redundant interface (class C implements A, B with A extends B) be visited twice; maxSpecific gets a duplicate and a unique default method resolves to None, so the callsite is not inlined or closure-rewritten. Verified with the repo's compiler jar: implements JB, JA inlines to bipush 42, implements JA, JB does not. Only Java/JDK classfiles under -opt-inline.

s2: n/a: port divergence; 2.13 uses transitive isSubtypeOf
what: Maximally-specific check only looks at direct superinterfaces (otherOwner.interfaces.contains(owner.name)). With JB{m}, JA extends JB, JD extends JA {m}, both stay in maxSpecific and resolution fails; final JF implements JD is not inlined. Scala-compiled hierarchies unaffected (mixin forwarders).

The clearMaxsComputed call is commented out and MethodMax has no clearing function, so cached maxLocals/maxStack stick after mutation. Audit found no current case where they end up too small; latent hazard.
AsmAnalyzer no longer computes maxs itself (every caller is guarded, fragile) and does not lift ASM 9.11's analyzer compute limits as 2.13 does. Likely unreachable under Scala 3's tighter Limits.

s2: 2.13 tracks indyLambdaImplMethods and builds $deserializeLambda$ after the optimizer
what: $deserializeLambda$ is built at codegen time, so an indy inlined into another class would be missing from that class's table. Masked today because lambda bodies are private static and the inliner refuses cross-class access.
no-inline-mixed warning setting is read but never used; ClassNotFound lost definedInJavaSource and its message.

s2: n/a: Scala 3-only, introduced by ff88d25f2b (2026-10-07, #27205); not fork debt
what: catch case e: RuntimeException if false =>: the wrapping of TASTy unpickling failures into a readable IOException (file path, version-too-old/new message) is disabled, so an UnpickleException surfaces raw. Looks like a debugging remnant. Confirmed in the worktree.

s2: scala/scala 34c9fb97e9 (2026-08, scala/bug#13152) freezes at 28.7; scala3 HEAD is 28.11-exp-1
what: Scala 2.13's reader is byte-for-byte in sync with Scala 3.7.x (diff -w clean from object TastyFormat down against 3.7.0 and 3.7.4) and deliberately rejects 28.8+. The 3.7.4 → 3.9.0 delta is only SUBMATCH=48 (MATCH flag) and INTO=49 (modifier tag, needs isModifierTag); neither name exists in Scala 2's TASTy sources. Policy debt, not drift: each Scala 3 minor needs a deliberate sync.

validOverride = possibles.isEmpty || ... with toolOverrides always empty made the header version gate a no-op in 2.13.13 through 2.13.18: the 2.13.18 jar accepts a 28.7 header above its own minor, so released 2.13 compilers try to read 3.8/3.9 TASTy and would hit assert(false, "illegal modifier tag") on INTO instead of a clean version error. Reproduced against the 2.13.18 jar.

s2: scala3 ecfa019360 (2026-04-17) "Fix infinite loop with bad section ends"
what: Unchecked toInt in readNat: a section length that decodes negative makes readSection goto backwards and loop forever on a corrupt .tasty. Reproduced with the real TastyReader from the 2.13.18 jar (1,000,000 iterations, isAtEnd still false).

s2: scala3 730eefa650 (2026-02-16) "Take JDK 9+ modules into account when determining what can be inlined"
what: 2.13's inliner access check only looks at ACC_PUBLIC, with a hard-coded jdk/internal/sun/ name list. Scala 3 reads module-info.class and marks only unconditionally exported packages accessible. With -opt:inline:**, inlining Objects.checkIndex compiles and fails at runtime with IllegalAccessError on jdk.internal.util.Preconditions. Reproduced on 2.13.19-M1.

0.toChar doubles as the skip sentinel for text-block line continuations, so a Java static final String read from source loses every NUL: "\0" becomes "", and the wrong constant is inlined into Scala callers. Scala 3 uses a separate skip flag. Checked against javac on ~50 literal forms; only this one differs. Reproduced.

Every NEW forces the full prod-cons analysis before checking which class is created; Scala 3 guards each arm with the box/Ref/Tuple constructor sets and adds a per-method analysis budget. The guards are a mechanical, output-preserving backport; the budget is a design change. Compile-time only, not benchmarked on 2.13.

-Yprofile-trace writes unescaped names into the JSON ("This assumes no escaping is needed"); a source file named a"b.scala yields a trace that json.load rejects. Scala 3 added JsonNameTransformer. Reproduced.

Class and jar writers follow symlinks at the output path: with out/Foo.class a symlink to target.txt, scalac -d out overwrites the target. Scala 3 deletes first and opens with NOFOLLOW_LINKS. Reproduced. (C5 notes the Scala 3 version's own race.)
UTF-8 string-too-large is detected correctly but reported as two position-less errors; Scala 3 checks at bytecode generation time and positions it.
